subject: Food Science
title: Retort Processing
description: A fast breakdown of Retort Processing for builders.

hook.text: A retort pouch looks like a flat bag but can withstand 121°C and 2 atmospheres of pressure. It replaces the can.

buildup.text: Retort processing heats sealed flexible pouches or trays to sterilization temperatures—same principle as canning.

discovery.text: Thinner packages heat faster. A retort pouch reaches sterility in half the time of a thick metal can.

twist.text: Less processing time means better color, texture, and nutrient retention. Retort-pouched tuna tastes noticeably fresher.

climax.text: MREs (Meals Ready to Eat) for the military use retort pouches. They last 5 years at 27°C without refrigeration.

punchline.text: Same heat, thinner package, shorter time, better food. The can evolved.

quiz.question: Why do retort pouches produce better quality food than cans?
options: Thinner pouches heat faster, reducing processing time and preserving quality
